pages.title: Asset Utilization Intelligence
pages.heroHeadline: Turn idle fleet capacity into productive output
pages.subtitle: See utilization, idle time, engine hours, and location in one view so you can redeploy underused assets, relieve overused ones, and stop paying for equipment that sits.

sections.title: Does this sound familiar?
bullets: Utilization looks fine in reports, but idle share stays high and cost per km keeps rising.
Underused assets are found too late because active/inactive and long-dwell signals are not monitored daily.
Mileage, engine hours, and duty status live in separate reports, so relocation decisions are delayed.
Non-contractual usage is suspected, but there is no clear contract-vs-actual evidence by asset.
Search time and queue time are not measured consistently, so capacity loss stays unclear.

sections.title: From fragmented fleet signals to one utilization decision model

cards.title: 1) Standardize baseline and custom KPIs
cards.text: Start with productive hours, engine hours, mileage, idle %, and active/inactive split. Add custom metrics: service-to-idle ratio, days-to-locate, queue time, and contract-vs-actual usage.

cards.title: 2) Detect underused, overused, and missing assets daily
cards.text: Rules and anomaly checks highlight idle over 72h, long dwell in depot, repeated idle without workload, and assets moving outside approved zones.

cards.title: 3) Convert signals into action decisions
cards.text: Planner chooses relocate, retire, rental substitution, billing correction, or process redesign by yard/shift based on impact and urgency.

sections.title: Use cases and decission patterns

cards.title: Public or enterprise fleet right-sizing
cards.text: Problem: Underused vehicles stay in service while budget requests for new assets continue.||Solution: Use odometer, engine hours, duty status, and equipment usage to identify structurally idle units and reassign or retire them before the next capex cycle.

cards.title: Rental and mixed-fleet optimization
cards.text: Problem: Portfolio-level averages hide non-contractual usage and margin leakage.||Solution: Compare productive hours, uptime, and contract-vs-actual behavior to relocate assets and apply chargeback where usage exceeds contract terms.

cards.title: Container and yard asset control
cards.text: Problem: Unauthorized movement and long dwell time remain invisible until claims or service failure.||Solution: Combine location, tamper/open events, and heartbeat freshness to trigger recovery actions, claims support, and detention-cost reduction.

sections.title: From trip signal noise to a delivery decision model

cards.title: 1) Normalize plan, progress, and integrity data
cards.text: Ingest route plan, stop list, time windows, location trace, dwell, assignment state, temperature, and door events under one trip ID.

cards.title: 2) Detect critical exceptions while the trip is active
cards.text: Flag missed checkpoint, ETA shift > threshold, dwell > SLA, route deviation, driver-not-logged-in, and reefer threshold breach.

cards.title: 3) Orchestrate action across dispatcher and back-office
cards.text: Send alerts to dispatch, create TMS/ERP issues automatically, and apply correction before SLA or product quality is lost.

sections.title: Use cases and decission patterns

cards.title: Assignment quality and fuel discipline
cards.text: Problem: Driver login mismatch and idling hide true trip accountability and inflate fuel cost.||Solution: Enforce assignment logic, combine idling and driver-behavior signals, and use route-level accountability reporting.

cards.title: ERP-synced trip execution control
cards.text: Problem: Trip plans live in one system while telematics events live in another, delaying response to deviations.||Solution: Sync plan/checkpoints with telematics, automate trip-event transfer to ERP/TMS, and trigger same-day deviation handling.

cards.title: Cold-chain delivery integrity
cards.text: Problem: Temperature excursions and door events are reviewed after spoilage risk and claim exposure.||Solution: Monitor temperature and door integrity during transit, link events to trip milestones, and build audit-ready evidence for claims.

sections.title: From event counts to risk decisions that reduce loss

cards.title: 1) Detect and classify safety-critical events
cards.text: Combine rules and video context for speeding, harsh maneuvers, distraction, seatbelt non-use, and collision proxies with one severity model.

cards.title: 2) Route each event into the right workflow
cards.text: Send evidence-backed incidents to claims/exoneration and behavioral patterns to coaching queue with clear owner, SLA, and escalation path.

cards.title: 3) Close the loop with measurable improvement
cards.text: Record coaching completion and driver acknowledgement, then monitor recurrence, claims outcomes, and risk score movement over time.

sections.title: Use cases and decission patterns

cards.title: Coaching-first safety transformation
cards.text: Problem: Event counting alone does not reduce incidents when feedback is delayed and generic.||Solution: Launch daily/weekly review by behavior segments, assign targeted coaching, and track recurrence after each intervention.

cards.title: Claims defense and driver exoneration
cards.text: Problem: Claims teams spend days reconstructing incidents with weak evidence quality.||Solution: Use dashcam footage plus event metadata as one evidence base, split exoneration branch from coaching branch, and reduce dispute cycle-time.

cards.title: Safety in remote and severe environments
cards.text: Problem: In low-connectivity regions, delayed alerts turn manageable risk into major incidents.||Solution: Configure priority notifications for severe conditions, support remote-area response patterns, and focus operations on time-to-intervention.

sections.title: From reactive repairs to maintenance decisions before failure

cards.title: 1) Convert raw service signals into one maintenance backlog
cards.text: Ingest OBD/CAN/J1939 fault data, odometer and engine hours, PM schedules, DVIR forms, and parts/labor records under one asset model.

cards.text: Use rule engine logic to group low-risk defects with upcoming PM, while opening urgent work orders for high-severity failures.

cards.title: 3) Close root cause and update lifecycle economics
cards.text: After repair, capture root-cause closure and feed cost plus downtime back into asset history for retention and replacement planning.

sections.title: How to choose the right BI tool for your team

cards.title: Power BI
cards.text: Best when Microsoft 365 integration, quick setup, enterprise support, and built-in refresh workflows matter most.

cards.title: Apache Superset
cards.text: Best for open-source flexibility, strong SQL workflows, and scalable multi-user analytics with technical ownership.

cards.title: Python + Streamlit
cards.text: Best for rapid custom prototypes, ML-centric analytics apps, and teams with strong Python engineering capacity.

cards.title: Grafana
cards.text: Best for operational monitoring, time-series dashboards, variable-based filtering, and real-time telemetry exploration.

sections.title: Connection playbooks for your first dashboard

cards.title: Power BI playbook
cards.text: Install Power BI Desktop, set DB parameters in report templates, configure credentials, and enable scheduled refresh in service.

cards.title: Superset playbook
cards.text: Deploy with Docker, add PostgreSQL SQLAlchemy URI with SSL=require, then import datasets/charts/dashboards in sequence.

cards.title: Grafana playbook
cards.text: Add PostgreSQL data source, use Code mode SQL queries, configure variables, and import dashboard JSON templates for faster rollout.

cards.title: Python + Streamlit playbook
cards.text: Create .env-based DB config, connect with psycopg2, and ship interactive analytics with rapid iteration and Python libraries.

sections.title: Sensoriqua: custom warehouse monitoring app

cards.title: 1) Problem
cards.text: Warehouse supervisors needed temperature and humidity control across 12 zones, trend investigation, and exception visibility, but fleet UI patterns were optimized for dispatch workflows.

sections.title: Trips Intelli: custom trip intelligence app

cards.title: 1) Problem
cards.text: Raw GPS points did not answer operational questions about trip quality, route adherence, overtime, suspicious behavior, and sensor integrity.

cards.title: 2) Custom solution
cards.text: Trips Intelli converts telemetry into a trips workspace with KPI strip, trip table, route map, status timeline, shift control, anomaly scoring, route-corridor deviation, and XLSX export.

cards.title: 3) Operational effect
cards.text: Dispatch, fleet managers, finance, and leadership get one evidence base for daily control, incident review, compliance checks, and management reporting.

sections.title: App Connect: embedded access inside navixy
sections.description: Navixy App Connect is an authentication middleware that securely bridges Navixy sessions and third-party apps, so custom tools open with existing credentials and inherited platform permissions.
kpiStrip: Session key to secure JWT token exchange
No separate passwords for custom tools
Secure data access through Navixy auth layer
Faster developer integration via standard contract

cards.title: Who gets value
cards.text: Developers ship integrations faster, admins control app access centrally, and end users open approved tools without extra logins.

cards.title: How it works in practice
cards.text: An external app requests App Connect auth, Navixy session is exchanged into JWT, and access is granted according to current Navixy permissions.

cards.title: Reference pattern
cards.text: Dashboard Studio demonstrates the same model: automatic session handoff, permission-aware data access, and continuous cross-app session continuity.

sections.title: Why is IoT Query database preferable compared to API?

cards.title: API access model
cards.text: Pagination and rate limits complicate long historical analysis.||Teams must build middleware, sync jobs, and local storage before analytics starts.||Tenant isolation and permission mapping often require custom backend logic.||Operational changes become integration projects instead of dashboard updates.

cards.title: SQL access with IoT Query
cards.text: One SQL-ready layer serves both real-time monitoring and historical investigation.||PostgreSQL-compatible queries remove the need for custom storage and aggregation services.||Existing org boundaries and filters support multi-tenant and branch-level views.||Teams focus on alerts, KPIs, and workflows instead of integration maintenance.
